Subject: MAP: Dedicated Capacity — throughput targets, roles & evaluation plan

Elaine, Samir —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As discussed, we're proposing a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to align on the Dedicated GPU pool commitment, target throughput, and the customer-run evaluation you'll run in your staging environment. The goal is a signed commitment and first-week validation run within six weeks.

Attached is a draft MAP (MAP_Nimbus_Dedicated_v1.pdf) and a one-sheet with recommended throughput targets (throughput_targets.xlsx). High level asks:
- Confirm primary stakeholders and an engineering lead for the validation run.
- Agree on target throughput SLOs (tokens/sec and p95 latency) for the pilot lane.
- Sign the MAP draft or suggest edits by EOD Friday so we can lock resource reservations.

Proposed kickoff agenda (30'): intros, scope, milestones, success criteria, immediate blockers. Proposed times: Tue 18 Aug, 10:00–10:30am PT or Wed 19 Aug, 2:00–2:30pm PT. Which works for your team?

I'll run the kickoff from our side. Dylan will coordinate model variants and evaluation checklist; Rishi will scope capacity targets; Marissa will handle billing/contract items. Vivek (cc'd on this thread separately) will join for any late-stage SLAs.

If you'd rather I send a short MAP tracker instead of the PDF for collaborative edits, tell me and I can share a Drive link.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales Lead — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: MAP_Nimbus_Dedicated_v1.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: throughput_targets.xlsx (XLSX)

--

Onboarding notes: the MAP draft includes a 3-phase plan: 1) Pilot validation (2 weeks), 2) Performance tuning & SLA baseline (2 weeks), 3) Commit & reserve capacity (ongoing). The evaluation checklist lists 12 test prompts and KV cache priming steps.

Laura —

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick questions from our side before the kickoff:
1) For the pilot validation, do you need us to provision a staging dataset or will Redwood use synthetic prompts?
2) The throughput spreadsheet lists a baseline of 18k tokens/sec for the 8xA100 pool — is that peak or sustained? We want to set realistic internal expectations.
3) Can you confirm what telemetry/logs are available during the validation? Our security team will want audit log access and example retention windows.

Stakeholders we tentatively plan to join:
- Elaine Park (PM, NimbusAI) — primary PO
- Samir Shah (CloudOps Lead) — infra/contact for capacity
- Priya Venkataram (SRE) — will confirm availability after internal sync

Thanks,
Elaine

elaine@nimbus.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@nimbus.ai>, Samir Shah <samir@cloudops.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Dedicated Capacity — throughput targets, roles & evaluation plan

All —

Punting answers to Elaine's questions here and adding a couple of internal items.

1) Dataset: We prefer Nimbus runs their real-ish staging dataset for fidelity. That said, we can seed the eval with a synthetic set to exercise KV-caching and long-context behaviour; your team should bring any specific prompts you want validated. See evaluation_checklist.md attached.

2) Throughput spreadsheet: the 18k tokens/sec is a sustained baseline for the pilot lane with continuous batching configured and KV cache hot. Peak throughput can be higher for short bursts. Rishi — can you confirm expected p95 latency for the baseline so we can land on acceptance criteria?

3) Telemetry: We’ll surface token-level latency, per-request model variant, GPU utilization, and exportable audit logs (retention: 90 days by default for the pilot). If Nimbus needs an extended retention window we can lock that in at commit.

Action items for our side before Wed:
- Rishi: populate latency targets into throughput_targets.xlsx (due Mon EOD).
- Marissa: draft a one-page commercial summary (commit levels + discount band) — attach to MAP v1.
- Laura: send calendar invite and attach Drive MAP tracker for collaborative edits.

I’m also adding a short section in the MAP about fallback policies (region failover and model variant fallback) so the pilot team understands graceful degradation during stress tests.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: evaluation_checklist.md (MD)

A few quick clarifications for the invite and kickoff:
- Meeting length: 30 minutes (we’ll keep tight).
- Deliverables by end of pilot: 1) throughput baseline report (xlsx) 2) 12-point evaluation pass/fail matrix (MD) 3) decision on capacity commit (yes/no) + preferred commit level.
- Success criteria: sustained tokens/sec within 85% of baseline and p95 < agreed latency target for 2 consecutive runs.
